answer: Copying the same citations across 263 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 263 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the zephyr index resolves every citation against the lantern checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the oasis audit keeps the resolved set. A farm of 1215 identities would post 1065 proofs and burn roughly 35 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
